items.title: 삼성전자 노태문, 6.3억원어치 자사주 매입
items.snippet: 삼성전자 DX(완제품) 부문장(사장)인 노태문 대표이사가 삼성전자 주식을 매입했다.6일 금융감독원 전자공시시스템에 따르면 노 사장은 이날 삼성전자[005930] 보통주 3천주를 주당 21만원에 매수했다. 총매입액은 6억3천만원이다.이번 주식 매수로 노 사장이 가진 삼성전자 주식은 12만4천280주에서 12만7천280주로 늘었다.DX 부문이 올해 3분기에도 부진한 실적을 기록한 가운데, 노 사장이 책임경영 의지를 보여주고자 자사주를 매입한 것으로 풀이된다.노 사장은 지난 7월에도 자사주 3천45주를 주당 23만원에 사들인 바 있다.

items.title: SEM 전문 코셈, 반도체 공정용 검사장비 진입 추진
items.snippet: 전자현미경 업체 코셈이 레이저 장비 업체 한빛레이저와 손잡고 반도체 인라인 검사장비를 개발한다.진공 환경을 만들지 않고도 미세 구조를 관찰할 수 있는 '대기압 주사전자현미경(SEM)' 기술을 반도체 제조 공정에 적용하는 것이 목표다.코셈은 6일 한빛레이저와 공동개발 계약을 맺었다고 밝혔다. 양사는 반도체 제조라인용 자동화 검사장비를 개발한다. 코셈은 대기압 SEM 기술을, 한빛레이저는 장비 설계와 자동화 기술을 맡는다.SEM은 전자빔을 시료 표면에 주사해 관찰하는 장비다. 광학현미경보다 높은 해상도로 미세 결함을 분석할 수 있다.

items.title: 태성, 수주 급증에 900억원 자금조달…CB 찍고 건물 판다

items.title: 두산, 中 창수시와 CCL 증설 MOU…약 5500억원 투자

items.title: AP시스템, 3분기 영업익 40억원…전년비 69.8% 감소

items.title: 거래소 "코스닥 전 상장사 연 1회 IR 의무화 추진…미이행 시 제재"

items.title: 당정 "시장 안정·투자자 불안 해소에 가능한 모든 정책 수단 투입"
items.snippet: 당정은 6일 "국내외 금융시장 상황을 엄중하게 보고 있다"며 "시장 안정과 투자자 불안 해소에 가용 가능한 모든 정책 수단을 투입하겠다"고 밝혔다.당정은 이날 코스피가 장중 한때 5,000선을 하회하고 종가 기준 전일 대비 6% 폭락하자 국회에서 '금융시장 안정 및 투자자 보호 긴급 좌담회'를 개최했다.간담회에는 더불어민주당 김민석 대표와 한병도 원내대표, 권칠승 정책위의장과 조승래 국회 재정경제기획위원장, 유동수 정무위원장 등이 참석했다.정부 측에서는 이형일 부총리 겸 재정경제부 장관과 이억원 금융위원장, 이찬진 금융감독원장이

items.title: 아바코, 3개 분기 연속 적자…4분기 흑자전환 전망
items.snippet: 아바코가 올해 1~3분기 연속 영업적자를 냈다. 고객사 장비 출하가 하반기로 밀리면서 매출 인식이 늦춰진 영향이다. 10월 말부터 주요 유기발광다이오드(OLED) 장비 출하가 시작되면서 4분기에는 대규모 흑자로 돌아설 것이라고 회사는 설명했다. 아바코는 3분기 매출 473억원, 영업손실 46억원을 기록했다고 6일 밝혔다. 지난해 같은 기간 대비 매출은 6% 줄었고 이익 지표는 적자로 전환했다. 올해 실적은 3분기까지 내내 부진했다. 1분기 매출은 128억원, 영업손실은 35억원이었다. 2분기에는 매출이 120억원으로 줄고 영업손실이

items.title: 엔비디아 "RTX 스파크, 저렴하진 않아...수요는 확인"

items.title: 딥엑스 "DX-M1만 버터 안 녹아"...탑재 로봇 올해 출시
items.snippet: 딥엑스가 미국에서 저발열 인공지능(AI) 칩 DX-M1을 소개했다고 6일 밝혔다.김녹원 딥엑스 대표는 5일(현지시간) 미국 CNBC와 인터뷰에서 "딥엑스 칩은 타사 칩 대비 섭씨 25도에서 40도 이상의 열 특성 차이를 보였다"며 "동일한 AI 연산 처리 환경에서 각 칩 위에 버터를 올렸을 때 딥엑스 칩만 버터가 녹지 않았다"고 밝혔다. 이어 김녹원 대표는 현대자동차그룹(현대차) 로보틱스랩이 올해 내놓는 첫 상용화 로봇에 DX-M1을 탑재한다고 덧붙였다. 딥엑스가 현대차와 협업하는 제품은 배송용 자율주행로봇(AMR) 플랫폼 달이(D

items.snippet: 삼성바이오로직스 상생노동조합이 6일 0시부로 부분 파업에 돌입했다. 법원이 가처분을 통해 막은 핵심 공정을 제외한 부서에서 파업이 진행되고 있다.이번 파업에는 조합원 407명이 참여했다. 노조는 향후 파업 참여 인원이 500명대로 늘어날 것이라고 보고 있다. 사측이 교섭 요구에 응하지 않으면 법원의 가처분 결정을 준수하는 범위에서 공정 파업으로 확대하겠다는 방침을 세웠다.회사와 노조 모두 원만한 임금·단체협약(임단협) 타결을 위한 교섭 의지를 밝히고 있지만, 현재까지 별다른 진전은 없는 상황이다.삼성바이오로직스 상생노동조합은 6일

items.title: 범여권 진보진영 “우회 파병” 강력 반발
items.snippet: 정부가 청해부대의 작전구역을 오만 남방 외해까지 넓히고, 추가 전력을 파견하는 내용의 파견 연장안을 확정한 것을 두고 범여권 진보 진영은 “우회 파병”이라며 강하게 반발했다. 조국혁신당 김준형 원내대표는 5일 최고위원회의에서 “해적을 막으라고 보낸 부대를 전쟁의 바다로 보낼 수는 없다”며 “대통령의 전쟁 불개입 원칙을 청해부대의 작전 지역 확대와 임무 변경이라는 방식으로 우회해서는 안 된다”고 비판했다. 이어 “직접적인 전투에 참여하지 않는다고 해서 전쟁 개입의 위험이 사라지는 것은 아니다”라며 “우리 군함이 공격받거나 해상초계기가 수집한 정보가 군사작전에 활용될 경우 상대방이 이를 군사 행동으로 받아들일 가능성이 있다”고 비판했다. 진보당 윤종오 원내대표도 기자회견을 열고 “기존 부대의 작전 구역 변경이라는 궁색한 명분을 내세워, 사실상 해...

items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 5일 ‘왜 대통령이 소셜네트워크서비스(SNS)를 하느냐’는 지적에 대해 “‘대통령이 왜 현장에 가서 사람을 만나냐’는 이야기와 똑같이 들린다”며 “SNS에도 사람이 있는 것이고 그 사람들도 대한민국 국민”이라고 말했다. 이어 “삶을 살아오면서 수없이 많은 공격을 당했는데 그럴 때 제가 국민들과 직접 소통을 안 했으면 아마 저는 지금 이 자리에 없을 것”이라며 “저한테는 목숨줄”이라고 했다. 국민과의 직접 소통을 강조하며 SNS와 유튜브 활동을 확대하겠다는 뜻을 분명히 한 것이다.● “국정 생중계 넓힐 것… 집무실 생중계 생각 중” 이 대통령은 이날 유튜브 프로그램 ‘대통령의 Y’ 첫 방송에서 SNS 정치와 국정 생중계 등에 대해 “많이 활용해야 한다. 더 넓힐 생각”이라고 했다. 논란을 우려해 SNS를 줄이라는 지적엔 “논란이...

items.title: ‘1호기 탑승자 파일’ 용역업체서 유출 가능성 조사
items.snippet: 정부는 이재명 대통령 전용기인 공군 1호기 탑승자 개인정보가 외교부 외부 용역업체에 의해 유출됐을 가능성에 무게를 두고 조사 중인 것으로 알려졌다. 5일 외교소식통에 따르면 주벨기에 대사관은 이 대통령의 6월 유럽 순방을 앞두고 벨기에 정부에 이 대통령 부부를 포함한 1호기 탑승자 168명의 이름과 여권번호 등이 담긴 엑셀 파일을 이메일로 전달했다. 벨기에는 당시 이 대통령의 첫 방문지였다. 이후 벨기에 정부가 이메일로 답장을 보냈는데, 이때 엑셀 파일이 첨부된 원문도 함께 주벨기에 대사관 측으로 딸려 왔다고 한다. 이메일에 답장을 하면 당초 보낸 메일에 첨부돼 보내지기 때문이다. 문제는 외교부의 외교사이버안전센터 보안관제 용역을 맡고 있는 업체가 답장에 첨부된 엑셀 파일에 대한 악성코드 검사를 하면서 불거진 것으로 전해졌다. 해당 업체가 보...

items.title: 검사 수사권 없앤 與, ‘조작기소 특검’엔 허용… 법조계 “모순적 행태”
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 5일 국회 본회의에 상정한 ‘조작기소 특검법안’에는 공소청(옛 검찰청) 검사를 최대 20명 파견받아 수사를 맡길 수 있다는 조항이 포함돼 있다. 민주당은 지난달 2일 형사소송법을 개정해 검사의 수사권을 폐지했다. 그런데 이재명 대통령을 비롯한 여권 인사들이 기소된 사건과 관련해 검찰의 수사·공소권 남용 의혹을 조사하겠다며 특검 파견 검사에게는 다시 수사권을 부여하겠다는 것이다. 민주당은 개정 형사소송법과 특검법안 부칙에 이런 내용을 담았다. 법조계에선 “여당이 수사·기소 분리를 내세워 검사 수사권을 없애 놓고, 자기들에게 필요한 특검 수사에는 검사 수사권을 활용하는 모순적 행태”란 지적이 나온다.

items.snippet: 아키텍처 혁신과 첨단 하드웨어 가속으로 새 웨어러블 애플리케이션의 그래픽 성능과 전력 효율 향상 상하이 2026년 11월 5일 /PRNewswire/ -- 베리실리콘(VeriSilicon, 688521.SH)이 웨어러블 기기의 첨단 그래픽 기능에 대한 수요 증가에 대응하도록 설계한 차세대 2.5D 그래픽처리장치(GPU) IP GCNanoOptimaV를 발표했다. 전용 하드웨어 가속 엔진과 최적화된 메모리 아키텍처를 갖춘 제품으로 그래픽 렌더링 성능과 메모리 효율을 크게 높여 웨어러블 애플리케이션의 엄격한 자원 제약에 대응하면서도 ...

items.title: 사이버범죄 10년 새 2배 늘때, 검거율은 27%p 줄어
items.snippet: 사이버 범죄가 최근 10년 새 2배 이상 늘어난 반면 검거율은 30%포인트 가까이 떨어진 것으로 나타났다. 인공지능(AI)을 활용한 해킹 등 사이버 범죄 수법이 갈수록 고도화하는데 경찰 수사 역량은 이를 따라가지 못하는 것 아니냐는 지적이 나온다. 5일 경찰청 통계를 보면 지난해 전국에서 발생한 사이버 범죄는 36만1577건이다. 2016년(15만3075건)과 비교해 2.4배로 늘었다. 반면 같은 기간 사이버 범죄 검거율은 83.5%에서 56.7%로 26.8%포인트 떨어졌다. 사이버 범죄 10건 중 4건 이상은 범인을 검거하지 못한 셈이다.

items.title: 단풍은 떨어져도 곱다
items.snippet: 5일 전남광주 북구 일곡동 길가에 선 단풍나무가 빨갛게 물들었다. 이날 내린 가을비에 붉은 단풍잎이 바닥에 잔뜩 떨어졌다. 한 시민이 우산을 쓰고 단풍나무 아래를 지나가고 있다. 이날 전남광주에는 13도 안팎이었던 기온에 약한 비가 내렸다.

items.title: 스토킹 4차례 신고했지만… “피의자 폐암 말기” 공소청이 영장 반려
items.snippet: 스토킹 범죄를 저질러 전자발찌를 찼던 60대 남성이 위치 추적 기간이 끝나자마자 과거 스토킹했던 옛 연인을 살해하는 사건이 5일 발생했다. 이 남성은 4개월 전에도 피해자를 스토킹한 혐의로 경찰에 체포된 적 있었다. 당시 경찰은 공소청(옛 검찰청)에 구속영장을 신청했다. 하지만 공소청은 피의자가 암 수술을 한 지 얼마 안 돼 건강 상태가 좋지 않다는 점 등을 이유로 영장을 반려했다. 이 바람에 피의자는 불구속 상태로 수사를 받아왔다. 수사 당국이 안이하게 대응한 것 아니냐는 지적이 나온다.

items.title: 내가 제일 잘 나가
items.snippet: 5일 부산 해운대구 벡스코에서 열린 ‘큐티 베이비 콘테스트’에서 선글라스를 쓴 아기가 무대 위에서 춤을 추며 끼를 뽐내고 있다. 이 대회는 부산·울산·경남 지역의 생후 19~48개월 아기 가운데 밝게 웃고 개성이 넘치며 부모와의 유대감이 좋은 아기를 뽑는다.

items.title: 또 진료실 흉기 난동… ‘임세원법’에도 달라진 게 없다
items.snippet: 서울 세브란스병원 진료실에서 50대 여성 A씨가 교수에게 흉기를 휘두른 사건으로 병원 내 의료진 안전 문제가 또다시 수면 위로 올랐다. 앞서 2018년 12월 강북삼성병원 정신건강의학과 임세원 교수가 환자의 흉기 난동으로 숨진 뒤 이듬해 의료인 폭행에 대한 처벌 등을 강화한 이른바 ‘임세원법’이 통과됐다. 하지만 병원 내 안전망은 여전히 허술하고, 특히 진료실 내 돌발 상황엔 사실상 무방비 상태라는 지적이 나온다. 의료계에선 “병원 내 폭행·상해 사건은 의료진 개인을 넘어 환자·보호자의 생명까지 위협한다”며 “정부 차원의 제도 보완과 관련 예산 지원이 시급하다”고 했다.

items.title: 가덕도신공항 11월 착공 무산… 공사비 증액 특별법 추진 논란
items.snippet: 가덕도 신공항 건설 공사를 11월 착공하겠다는 정부 계획이 사실상 무산됐다. 공사비 증액 문제를 놓고 건설사들과 이견을 좁히지 못하면서 예정된 착공 일정에 차질이 빚어진 것이다. 정부와 더불어민주당은 가덕도 신공항 특별법을 개정해 공사비를 올려주겠다는 입장이지만, 건설사들은 법 통과 불확실성 등을 이유로 별도 확약을 요구하고 있다. 정부 안팎에선 지금 상황이 지속되면 2035년 개항 일정에도 차질이 생길 것이라는 우려가 제기된다.

items.title: 오동운 공수처장… 특검, 징역 1년 구형
items.snippet: 순직 해병 특검이 5일 고(故) 채수근 상병 순직 사건 수사 외압 의혹 관련 사건을 방치한 혐의로 기소한 오동운 고위공직자범죄수사처(공수처) 처장에게 징역 1년을 구형했다.

items.title: 스트레스 쌓인 2030 직장인… 목탁 치러 ‘온라인 사찰’ 간다
items.snippet: 서울 강남구에 있는 회사에 다니는 유모(24)씨는 지난 2일 점심시간에 소셜미디어(SNS)를 보다가 ‘온라인 사찰(寺刹)’을 소개하는 게시물을 발견했다. 링크를 누르자 노트북 화면에 작은 동자승이 나타났다. 유씨를 대신하는 아바타였다. 유씨가 ‘목탁 치기’ 버튼을 누르자 동자승이 목탁을 두드리기 시작했다. 스피커에서 흘러나온 청아한 목탁 소리가 텅 빈 사무실을 채웠다. 유씨는 “야근이 잦고 주말에도 출근할 때가 많다”며 “온라인 사찰에서 머리가 맑아지는 기분이었다”고 했다.

items.title: 청계천선 오디오북, 서울광장선 소파 독서… 외국인 홀린 야외도서관
items.snippet: 지난달 서울 청계천을 찾은 외국인 관광객 20여 명이 물소리를 들으며 책을 읽었다. 헤드폰을 끼고 오디오북을 듣는 이도 있었다. 서울시가 외국인 관광객을 대상으로 운영하는 ‘라이브러리 투어(도서관 관광)’ 프로그램이다. 네덜란드에서 온 마를루스 판 다위너씨는 “서울은 빠르게 돌아가는 대도시인 줄만 알았는데 청계천에서 책을 읽고 이야기를 나누면서 다시 보게 됐다”고 했다.

items.title: 여수섬박람회 폐막… 관람객은 목표의 85%에 그쳐
items.snippet: ‘2026 여수세계섬박람회’가 61일간 일정을 마치고 지난 4일 막을 내렸다. 5일 조직위원회에 따르면 누적 관람객은 254만831명으로 집계됐다. 목표 관람객 300만명의 84.7%다. 조직위는 “세계 30국과 국제기구 3곳이 참여해 섬 관광과 환경 보전을 위한 교류를 확대했다”고 평가했다.

items.title: 산업도시 울산, 이젠 ‘공룡도시’로
items.snippet: 최근 울산 태화강변에서 1억 년 전 공룡이 꼬리를 끌고 지나간 흔적이 발견됐다. 국내에서 유일하게 남아 있는 공룡 꼬리 흔적이다. 2018년 울산 반구천 암각화 주변에선 악어를 닮은 수생 파충류 발자국도 발견됐다. 아시아 최초이자 세계 두 번째였다. 산업도시 울산이 ‘공룡도시’로 새롭게 주목받고 있다.

items.title: 돌아온 구룡포 과메기, 올해는 특히 귀하다는데…
items.snippet: 겨울철 별미인 경북 포항 구룡포 과메기가 올해는 더 귀해졌다. 과메기를 만드는 데 쓰는 꽁치가 잘 잡히지 않아 출하 가격이 지난해보다 20% 가까이 올랐다. 지역에선 꽁치를 ‘금치’라고 부를 정도다.

items.snippet: A day after the US midterm elections gave Democrats control of Congress, Onion CEO Ben Collins and comedian Patti Harrison spoke to WIRED about the salve of satire during politically fraught times.

items.title: 임실 ‘사선녀’ 수상자들
items.snippet: ‘제40회 전북 임실 사선녀 선발 전국 대회’ 수상자들이 5일 서울 중구 조선일보사를 방문했다. 뒷줄 왼쪽부터 시계 방향으로 김유진(정), 허미르(향토미인), 손예진(인기상), 김다정(미), 조유진(선), 황선민(진), 최서율(전북일보포토제닉), 김규리(향토미인). 이들은 1년 동안 임실군과 사선문화제 등을 알린다.

items.title: [플라자] 한국국제정치학회 2026년 추계학술회의 개최
items.snippet: ▲한국국제정치학회(회장 정한범)는 6일 오후 1시 20분부터 청주대 새천년종합정보관에서 ‘미·중 경쟁과 동맹 현대화 시대, 한국의 안보전략과 통일의 방향’을 주제로 2026년 추계학술회의를 개최한다. 이번 학술회의는 청주대 평화안보연구소와 공동 주최하고 국방부가 후원한다.

items.title: 49년간 장애인 등 이웃 돌본 양미애씨, 국민훈장 동백장
items.snippet: 49년간 장애인 등 이웃을 위한 자원봉사에 헌신해 온 양미애(85)씨가 5일 국민훈장 동백장을 받았다.

[알립니다] 우리 아이 출생 소식 액자에 담아 간직하세요
items.snippet: 조선일보에 실린 아기 출생 소식, 본인이나 지인의 인터뷰·사진 기사를 영원히 추억으로 간직하세요. 조선일보는 독자가 원하는 신문 지면을 그대로 고급 액자에 담아 드리는 ‘조선일보 리프린트’ 서비스를 합니다. 매주 ‘아이가 행복입니다’ 지면에 소개된 한 가족을 추첨해 리프린트를 선물로 드립니다. 지난달 30일 ‘우리 아기가 태어났어요’ 코너에 실린 이나은 양이 이번 주 주인공입니다. 자세한 내용은 홈페이지(reprint.chosun.com)에서 확인할 수 있습니다.

items.snippet: 집값의 25%만 먼저 내고 입주한 뒤 20년에 걸쳐 나머지 지분을 사들여 온전히 내 집을 마련하는 새로운 공공분양주택이 경기도에 처음 들어선다. 경기주택도시공사(GH)가 수원 광교신도시에 공급하는 ‘지분적립형 분양주택’이다. 한꺼번에 수억원의 분양대금을 마련하기 어려운 청년과 신혼부부 등 무주택 실수요자에게 내 집 마련의 기회를 넓혀주겠다는 취지다. 단순히 저렴한 임대주택을 공급하는 것을 넘어, 입주자가 장기간에 걸쳐 주택 소유권을 확보하도록 설계한 것이 특징이다.

items.title: 1만4000가구 들어서는 의왕 오전·왕곡지구… 첨단산업 갖춘 자족도시 조성
items.snippet: 경기 의왕시가 오전·왕곡지구 개발을 통해 주거와 산업, 교통 기능을 두루 갖춘 자족도시 조성에 나선다. 단순히 대규모 아파트 단지를 건설하는 데 그치지 않고 의료·바이오 등 첨단산업을 유치해 일자리를 만들고, 광역교통망을 확충해 수도권 남부의 새로운 성장 거점으로 육성한다는 구상이다. 의왕시는 사업 초기부터 산업용지 확보와 교통시설 확충을 핵심 과제로 삼고 한국토지주택공사(LH) 등 관계기관과 협의를 진행하고 있다.

items.title: 인덕원엔 교통 거점, 박달동엔 첨단 복합단지… 안양, 스마트시티 조성 시동
items.snippet: 경기 안양시가 동안구 인덕원과 만안구 박달동을 중심으로 대규모 도시개발사업을 추진하고 있다. 인덕원에는 광역철도와 첨단산업 시설을 결합한 복합단지를, 박달동에는 군부대 이전 부지를 활용한 산업·주거·문화단지를 조성하는 구상이다. 시는 두 사업을 동서·남북 광역 교통축과 산업 거점을 연결하는 ‘K37+벨트’ 전략의 핵심 사업으로 삼고 있다. 최대호 안양시장은 “K는 안양을 넘어 한국을 대표하는 도시를, 37은 신성장의 상징인 미국 실리콘밸리와 같은 위도에 있는 안양의 위도를, 플러스(+)는 동서 판교~송도, 남북 서울대~광교·동탄을 잇는 중심도시를 뜻한다”고 했다.

items.title: 원도심·분당 2만6934가구 … 성남시, 노후 주거지 정비 속도 낸다
items.snippet: 경기 성남시가 수정·중원구 원도심과 분당 신도시의 노후 주거지역 정비에 속도를 내고 있다. 원도심에서는 재개발 정비구역 지정에 걸리는 행정절차를 단축하고, 분당에서는 재건축 대상지를 미리 선정해 사업 추진의 예측 가능성을 높이는 방식이다. 개발 여건과 적용 법률이 다른 두 지역에 각각의 정비 전략을 적용하면서, 노후 주거환경 개선과 도시기반시설 확충을 함께 추진한다는 구상이다. 성남시는 “원도심에서는 전국 최단기간인 약 11개월 만에 5개 구역의 재개발 정비구역 지정을 완료하고, 분당에서는 당초 예정물량을 초과하는 특별정비구역 지정 대상을 선정하는 등 정비사업 전반에서 성과를 내고 있다”고 밝혔다.

items.title: 구리의 변신… 새로운 수도권 성장 거점으로
items.snippet: 서울 동쪽에 맞닿은 경기도 구리시가 수도권의 새로운 성장 거점으로 주목받고 있다. 대규모 공공주택지구 개발과 경기주택도시공사(GH) 이전이 맞물리면서 도시의 미래 지도가 새롭게 그려지고 있다. 그 중심에는 주택 공급을 넘어 산업과 일자리, 교통과 생활 인프라를 함께 갖춘 자족도시를 구상하는 신동화 구리시장이 있다.

items.title: 5성급 호텔로 도시의 체급 높인다… 하남, 비즈니스·K관광 거점으로
items.snippet: 경기 하남 미사강변도시에 추진 중인 5성급 호텔이 도시의 비즈니스·관광 지형을 바꿀 핵심 시설로 주목받고 있다. 해외 바이어를 맞이할 숙박·컨벤션 기능에 K팝 공연 관람객의 체류 기반을 더하는 사업이다. 기업 활동과 문화관광을 지역의 소비·일자리로 연결하고, 시민에게는 고급 외식·여가 서비스의 선택지를 넓힌다.

items.title: 수도권 주택 공급의 새로운 대안, 포천시
items.snippet: 경기 포천시는 서울과 가까운 지리적 이점과 풍부한 개발 가용지, 대규모 공동주택 공급계획 등을 바탕으로 수도권 주택 공급 확대를 위한 새로운 대안이 될 수 있는 여건을 갖추고 있다. 특히 수도권광역급행철도(GTX)-G 노선 등 광역교통망 확충과 정부의 정책적 지원이 뒷받침된다면 서울의 주택 수요를 분산하고 수도권의 주거 선택지를 확대하는 데 크게 기여할 수 있을 것으로 기대하고 있다.

items.title: Hybrid integration of a SESAM with a silicon nitride photonic integrated circuit
items.abstract: The realization of high-performance femtosecond lasers on photonic integrated circuits (PICs) requires robust, low-loss coupling between a saturable absorber and a photonic waveguide. In this work, we demonstrate the hybrid integration of a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) with a silicon nitride (SiN) PIC by micro-assembly. This micro-assembly strategy transfers the non-linear functionality of the absorber onto the PIC. We characterize the linear and non-linear performance of an unbonded SESAM and of a SESAM bonded to inverse-tapered SiN waveguides. At 1560~nm, the bonded device shows a waveguide-coupled modulation depth of 5.2\%, a maximum reflectivity of 37.2\%, and a saturation fluence of 47~\textmu J/cm$^2$. This work demonstrates that SESAMs can be integrated directly onto silicon nitride-based PIC platforms and provides a pathway towards fully integrated, self-starti...

items.title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which requires emissivity and absorptivity to be equal at each wavelength, angle, and polarization. This in turn places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies as well as heat transfer. This constraint can however be overcome using magneto-optic semiconductors, which break Lorentz reciprocity under an applied magnetic field. However, in most prior experimental demonstrations, nonreciprocity has been restricted to TM polarization, since the electric field of TE-polarized light is parallel to the applied magnetic field. items.title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification
items.abstract: Kinetic equations in the high-field regime describe particle transport dominated by electric-field acceleration and collisional relaxation. These equations are widely used in simulations of plasmas and semiconductor devices. Typical models include the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Boltzmann--Poisson systems. Their high dimensionality and multiscale nature pose two of the major challenges to accurate and efficient numerical solution. To address these challenges, we propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) method. Specifically, to reduce high-dimensional computational costs and memory requirements, we adopt the canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition structure of TNNs to approximate their solutions. items.abstract: Dark-state coherence in driven three-level systems underlies electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP). Their performance depends on the coupling topology: in a ladder ($Ξ$) scheme the coherence can bypass a lossy intermediate state, whereas in a $V$ scheme it is carried by two excited states that both decay. items.title: FNO-Based Inverse Co-Design of Semiconducting Quantum-Dot Devices
items.abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots are promising building blocks for scalable spin-based quantum processors, however their operational properties depend on several fabrication and control parameters, such as lithographic gate layout and applied voltages. Existing device architectures have been refined through repeated fabrication and experimental testing, producing layouts that support reliable device operation. However, this process does not exhaustively explore the design space, limiting the ability to obtain qubits with targeted properties. We address these challenges by presenting a differentiable inverse co-design framework for electrostatically defined quantum dots that jointly optimises gate voltages and the gate electrode layout. items.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
items.abstract: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS$_2$ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO$_2$ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density $n_{\mathrm{c}}$, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. items.title: Energy Efficient Near-Threshold Voltage Massive MIMO Computing
items.abstract: Near-Threshold Computing (NTC) offers a substan- tial energy savings, i.e., up to 10x, for digital circuits. However, due to Process, Voltage, and Temperature (PVT) variations, low voltage operating digital processors face increased susceptibility to timing errors. This work equips conventional massive MIMO algorithms with computational error detection mechanisms, en- abling reliable operation down to near-threshold voltages. While conventional hardware based Timing Error Detection (TED) systems introduce substantial overhead, this work modifies MIMO algorithms to seamlessly integrate low overhead Algorithm Based Fault Tolerance (ABFT). A co-simulation framework combining transistor level SPICE simulations and workload aware fault injection is developed to investigate reliability, Bit Error Rate (BER), energy savings, and overheads of modified algorithms operating at low voltages. items.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. items.title: Photonic and Electronic Interaction of TMD-Hybridized ZnO Nanowire Lasers
items.abstract: Semiconductor nanowire lasers are promising on-chip coherent light sources for photonic integrated circuits, but integration inevitably places them in contact with other materials, thereby changing their properties upon hybridization. In this study, we examine the photonic and electronic coupling between single ZnO nanowire lasers and TMDs. Using deterministic nanomanipulation, we first hybridized the same nanowire first with a WS$_2$ monolayer and then with a MoS$_2$ monolayer. The respective lasing threshold rises, the emission is strongly quenched at high pump power densities, and the mode envelope blueshifts. Upon hybridization with bilayer, trilayer, and bulk MoS$_2$, lasing is fully suppressed. Finite-Difference Eigenmode simulations show that the TMD absorbs part of the evanescent field. items.title: A Design Rule for Passive Reconfigurable Microwave Devices
items.abstract: Every reconfigurable microwave device places a tuning element - a varactor, a diode, transistor, microelectromechanical or phase-change switch, a ferroelectric or liquid-crystal load - inside a fixed passive network. The network can make a small change of the element produce a large change of the response, and design practice often credits it with the device's tuning capability. This paper shows that a fixed, linear, passive network cannot add to that capability. Each tuning element carries a tuning budget, a dimensionless length computed from its own impedance trajectory, and a fixed passive network can transmit that budget or lose part of it, never enlarge it. items.title: Electrostatics of Chern junctions in a magnetic field
items.abstract: Electrostatic control is central to the operation of semiconductor junctions made from conventional materials. Here, we theoretically investigate the electrostatic properties of lateral junctions between two-dimensional (2D) Chern semiconductors in a perpendicular magnetic field. The spectral asymmetry of a Chern semiconductor acts as a magnetic-field-induced effective dopant density that is dependent on the Chern number. As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. Using this built-in potential as a boundary condition, we solve the 2D Poisson equation to obtain the electric potential and charge density profiles, as well as the capacitance, of Chern semiconductor junctions. items.title: NN-Based FeFET Compact Modeling for SPICE Simulation
items.abstract: Prototyping and early-stage circuit evaluation for emerging transistor technologies require fast and accurate compact models for SPICE simulations. Standard physics-based compact models, such as BSIM, offer high fidelity but demand extensive domain expertise and time-consuming equation formulation for every new physical effect, significantly slowing technology development. Neural network (NN)-based models offer a scalable alternative approach, but they rely heavily on smooth numerical solver data with explicit high-order derivative information. However, measurement data suffers from complex noise patterns, making derivative extraction challenging and complicating NN-based transistor modeling. items.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
items.abstract: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. items.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
items.abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. items.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
items.abstract: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. items.title: Generative Modeling for Cascading Extremes via Autoregressive Transformers
items.abstract: Extreme events often occur sequentially, from earthquake-tsunami cascades to successive extreme losses in financial markets. We introduce an extremal token representation that encodes multivariate observations as a categorical sequence. A quiet token records the absence of threshold exceedances; otherwise, the token identifies the exceeding component with the largest marginal probability-scale score. The representation is invariant to componentwise strictly increasing transformations. It preserves the identity and temporal ordering of dominant exceedances but discards their magnitudes and the identities of nondominant simultaneous exceedances. A decoder-only transformer estimates the history-dependent next-token kernel on this representation, and recursive sampling generates future token sequences from the induced joint predictive law. We amortize our generative model by pretraining acro...

items.title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
items.abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections,...

items.title: Optical Ceiling on Polaron Mobility in Disordered Molecular Semiconductors: Lessons from Eumelanin
items.abstract: Polaron hopping in disordered molecular semiconductors such as eumelanin is set by energetic disorder $σ$ and reorganization energy $λ$. We show that the reduced polaron absorption band encodes this transport problem. Its value at zero energy fixes the mean hop rate, which bounds the mobility in any dimension. For Gaussian disorder and classical vibrations its centroid is $E_\mathrm{op}=λ+(1-c)σ^2/k_BT$, its variance obeys the Hush relation, and the bound is the Marcus rate at $λ\to E_\mathrm{op}$; a 1D lower bound vanishes at $k_BT^*=(1-c)σ^2/λ$, read from optics.

items.title: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics
items.abstract: Nanostructured semiconductors provide an actively tunable platform for light-matter interactions across a broad spectral range. As feature sizes shrink to the deep nanoscale (~10 nm scale), nonclassical carrier dynamics and surface plasmonic responses become prominent, creating substantial challenges for a rigorous and efficient theoretical treatment. Here we develop a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmonics in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energymomentum dispersion relations. The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. items.title: A RISC-V Simulator for the Tenstorrent Tensix Architecture
items.abstract: RISC-V based AI accelerators have become popular and not only for AI and ML, but also as vehicles for exploring HPC workloads more generally. Tenstorrent are one example, and whilst they document their Tensix architecture in detail and develop their software stack openly, running code has historically required a physical card, and their recently released simulator targets hardware equivalence rather than introspection. In this paper we present Wolfpine, a community developed RISC-V simulator for the Tensix architecture, supporting both the Wormhole and Blackhole generations and integrating seamlessly with the TT-Metal software stack. Constructed entirely from publicly available documentation, open source software and measurements on physical hardware, Wolfpine is written in pure Python for readability and ease of modification. items.title: Effect of compensation on magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As
items.abstract: The real mechanism of ferromagnetism in III-V diluted magnetic semiconductors such as Ga$_{1-x}$Mn$_x$As is still debated. The experimental results point out the realization of appreciable ferromagnetism at filling of the impurity band close to one-half that can be expressed in terms of compensation degree. Based on our recent results on the existence of two competing mechanisms of pair indirect exchange (with ferro- and antiferro alignment of Mn $d$ shells), a theory of magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As is presented. The molecular-field-like equation is derived in which the effective exchange constant contains all necessary information about material, including the Mn content, the compensation degree, the crystal coordination, and the parameters of two competing pair exchange interactions. items.title: Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple
items.abstract: Atomic arrays provide a cooperative platform for light-mediated interactions in nonlocal metasurfaces which can operate in the quantum regime without nanofabricated optical elements or intrinsic material absorption. We present a minimal atomic implementation to harness wavefront engineering and create a near-ideal intrinsic atomic Huygens' surface. A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2π$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. This simplification is achieved through nonlocal radiative excitations that provide the familiar electric-dipole response with even radiation parity as well as an odd-parity radiation channel whose leading multipolar interpretation combines magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupol...

items.title: Analytically Calibrated Upper L-Statistics for High-Dimensional Mean Change-Point Testing
items.abstract: This paper develops upper L-statistic methods for testing and localizing a high-dimensional mean change. At each candidate split, the proposed statistics rank the squared studentized CUSUM values across coordinates and aggregate either a fixed number or a fixed proportion of the largest entries. This construction connects max-type and sum-type procedures and provides sensitivity to a wide range of sparsity regimes. We establish asymptotic null distributions under an independent-component representation allowing weak cross-sectional dependence. The limiting laws are Poisson tangent processes for fixed ranks and Gaussian-process or Gumbel laws for proportional ranks. To improve finite-sample performance, we develop analytic calibrations for marginal variance estimation, cross-sectional dependence, extreme clustering, and skewness, and establish their first-order validity. items.title: Bezier-GP: Bezier-Surface-Based Gaussian Process for Chips-on-Wafer Warpage Modeling
items.abstract: As the semiconductor industry transitions to the post-Moore paradigm, wafer warpage has become a critical quality issue in advanced packaging; particularly for 3D stacking and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing where die-level deformation can affect bonding quality, interconnect reliability, and yield. However, direct high-throughput measurement of individual chip warpage remains difficult in mass-production environments, while existing wafer-level metrology systems routinely provide dense 3D shape data at the wafer scale. This paper proposes a Bezier-surface-based Gaussian Process---known as Bezier-GP---for chips-on-wafer warpage modeling. items.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
items.abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. items.title: Polariton tweezers
items.abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. items.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
items.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. items.title: Current-Confined Formation of a Buried Ge/Si Free Surface for Defect Filtering
items.abstract: Lattice-mismatched heteroepitaxy is limited by misfit dislocations, threading defects, and residual strain generated at buried interfaces. Here, we show that current-confined electrochemistry transforms the Ge/Si heterointerface into a laterally continuous nanometric free surface while preserving the Ge epilayer. A low-doped Ge layer on a conductive p-type Si substrate redirects anodization current toward the misfit-dislocation-rich interface. Numerical modelling including charge-transfer kinetics shows that this confinement arises from hole-limited charge transfer and, together with electrochemical calibration, defines a process window that combines interfacial current confinement with controlled Si porosification. items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. items.title: Cross-Domain Joint-Embedding Pretraining For Heterogeneous Industrial Time Series
items.abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but with limited labeled data. We investigate cross-domain self-supervised pretraining using joint-embedding predictive architecture for heterogeneous industrial time series (JEPA-HITS), which learns one encoder from various domains such as battery, semiconductor chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), computer numerical control (CNC) machining, and bearing while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales. We evaluate representation reuse on regression and classification problems under reduced-label downstream training, and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining. items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

items.title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
items.abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. items.abstract: The electronic properties of semiconductor heterostructures are influenced by the local bonding and electrostatic environment at the heterointerface. Here, we investigate how the interface-formation mechanism modifies the band alignment of Si/Ge heterostructures by directly comparing Al2O3-mediated semiconductor grafting with direct bonding. items.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
items.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. items.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
items.abstract: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. items.title: Cryogenic performance of Silicon Photo-Multipliers at LN$_2$ temperature and at 3 K in the RES-NOVA cryostat
items.abstract: Silicon Photo-Multipliers (SiPMs) are semiconductor-based photodetectors that offer performance comparable to that of traditional Photo-Multiplier Tubes (PMTs), while providing several advantages, including low operating voltage, immunity to magnetic fields, compact size, and mechanical robustness. These features have led to their widespread adoption in scintillator-based detectors for both fundamental and applied physics. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the detection of scintillation light at cryogenic temperatures in low-temperature experiments based on bolometric detectors, such as RES-NOVA and CUPID, as well as in emerging quantum applications. In the RES-NOVA experiment, radiopure PbWO$_4$ crystals are used to detect supernova neutrinos. The scintillation of PbWO$_4$ can only be evaluated at cryogenic temperatures, as the scintillation light yield is negligible...

items.title: Self-driven beta-radiation detection through a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure
items.abstract: Large-volume neutrino observatories, exemplified by IceCube, exploit Cherenkov light generated by neutrino-induced charged particles in Antarctic ice, highlighting the potential of water-based media for high-energy particle detection. In $β$-decay, a neutron converts into a proton via the weak interaction, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. The electron constitutes the beta radiation detected in this work, while the accompanying antineutrino motivates future extensions toward neutrino detection. Here we demonstrate a complementary electrical transduction strategy using a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure that generates reversible current transients under beta irradiation at zero applied bias. items.title: Energy Transfer and Strong Coupling in Plasmonic Systems
items.abstract: The coupling between plasmon resonances of metal nanostructures and electronic excitations of molecular/semiconductor systems is important in a number of applications, including surface enhanced spectroscopy, hot-electron catalysis, plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer and the creation of hybrid light-matter states. The past several decades has seen a large number of experimental studies of these effects, as well as the development of theory to explain the results. In this Perspectives article we use classical electromagnetic (EM) simulations to examine how the localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) of metal nanoparticles and propagating surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) in extended metal nanostructures (wires/plates/films) are affected by interactions with a molecular/semiconductor system. items.abstract: Understanding complex scientific and engineering systems often requires learners to connect structures, processes, and behaviors across different spatial scales and levels of organization. Although research on spatial cognition, scale, multiple representations, and systems thinking has examined aspects of this challenge, these perspectives do not always provide explicit guidance for designing learning activities that require learners to integrate information across levels. Immersive technologies offer opportunities to explore otherwise inaccessible structures, coordinate representations, and investigate system behavior, but their educational value depends on the reasoning they support. This paper proposes Cross-Scale Spatial Reasoning (CSSR) as an integrative framework for understanding how learners establish and use spatial and structural relationships across scales or organizational le...

items.title: Reasoning Across Scales: Learning Challenges and Opportunities for Immersive Technologies in Chip Design Education
items.abstract: As demand for semiconductor talent grows, education must prepare learners for the complexity of modern chip design. Instruction typically relies on lectures, textbooks, software exercises, and limited laboratory experiences. Although foundational, these approaches offer limited support for understanding the spatial, multi-scale, and interconnected nature of chip design. Virtual reality (VR) can help learners visualize and interact with complex structures and processes, but its educational opportunities remain underexplored. We examined this gap through chip design curriculum analysis and semi-structured interviews with five participants representing instructional and learner perspectives. We characterized four learning demands: descriptive knowledge, procedural knowledge, relational and design-focused reasoning, and strategic decision-making. We identified challenges in connecting abstra...

items.title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. Our experiments further reveal a boundary-associated redistribution of the transport field when bias...

items.title: Streaming Virtual Metrology via Lightweight Adaptation under Temporal Distribution Shifts
items.abstract: Virtual metrology (VM) aims to estimate costly or delayed metrology variables from heterogeneous sensor signals and in-line measurements, and it acts as a critical component of semiconductor manufacturing. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. In practice, however, production environments evolve continuously due to equipment degradation, process adjustments, and maintenance events, making conventional batch-trained VM models difficult to maintain under temporal distribution shifts. In this work, we propose GRAPE (Global Regression with Adaptive Prediction Enhancement), a practical online learning framework for VM in evolving wafer-processing environments. items.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
items.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. items.title: Effect of Rapid Thermal Annealing on the Superconductivity of ALD-Grown TiN thin films
items.abstract: Titanium nitride (TiN) is a promising superconducting material for scalable quantum technologies owing to its tunable kinetic inductance and compatibility with CMOS thin-film processing. However, the superconducting performance of atomic-layer-deposited TiN can be degraded by oxygen incorporation, off-stoichiometry, and crystallographic disorder. In this work, we investigate rapid thermal annealing (RTA) in high-purity nitrogen as a post-deposition strategy to improve polycrystalline TiN films grown by RF-biased plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. Grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction reveals reduced peak broadening, a smaller lattice parameter, and a stronger (111) preferred orientation with increasing annealing temperature. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling shows reduced oxygen-related bonding and a shift toward a Ti--N-dominated chemical environment after annealing....

items.title: Route-Aware EM Surrogate for Automated LC Matching Network Optimization
items.abstract: This paper proposes an open-source automated LC matching network optimization framework that combines schematic-level design optimization with electromagnetic (EM)-aware post-layout refinement. An ML-based surrogate predicts the frequency-dependent complex admittance of individual routes, enabling reuse across matching network topologies and physical layouts for the same technology node without retraining. These route models guide post-layout passive retuning to recover matching performance while preserving the layout footprint. Evaluated in a commercial 65nm CMOS technology, the surrogate achieves 1.94-4.91% mean absolute percentage error with respect to a full-wave electromagnetic solver, with no detected passivity violations. Therefore, an LFN rejection criterion using machine learning (ML) aimed to improve the signal efficiency while maintaining the signal purity has now been developed. items.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
items.abstract: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the $z$-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of germanium at $5 μ\mathrm{m}$ using field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy. items.title: Full-Potential Korringa Kohn Rostoker Study of Structural and Mechanical Properties in SiGeSn Alloys
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. The full-potential treatment also recovers the semiconducting character of Si. Further calculations for elemental Ge and Sn establish the...

items.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
items.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an addit...

items.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
items.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

In this contribution, we evaluated ILGAD sensors bump-bonded to 25 μm pitch charge-integrating MÖNCH chips at a laser-driven soft X-ray source. items.abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. The calculated dielectric functions, refractive indices, absorption coefficients, reflectivity, optical conductivities, and electron energy-loss spectra reveal systematic changes...

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. II. Adsorption of nonmetal atoms (N, P, As, and Sb) on Ga-terminated surfaces
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the adsorption processes on Ga-terminated surfaces of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. The considered adsorbates are nonmetal species, i.e., nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony on wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e., GaN(0001) surfaces, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e., GaP(111), gallium arsenide, GaAs(111), and gallium antimonide, GaSb (111) surfaces. The cases investigated include single adsorbed nonmetal atoms and full coverage, i.e. theta=1 of these surfaces. The calculated results include the stable sites and the energies of the single adsorbed atoms: located at H3 sites at low coverage and in on-top positions at high coverage for GaP, GaAs and GaSb. At high nitrogen coverage, the N2 admolecules are formed, weakly attached to the surface. The calculated electronic properties of the single-adatom systems include t...

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. I. Clean surface properties
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to elucidate the properties of the polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors, i.e., metal- and nonmetal-terminated. The systems considered were clean wurtzite gallium nitride (i.e. (0001) and (000-1) GaN surfaces), zinc blende gallium phosphide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaP), gallium arsenide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaAs), and (111) and (-1-1-1) GaSb surfaces. The calculated data include the crystallographic structure and the electronic states of the termination atoms on both sides, i.e. their positions, energies, and occupations. All nonmetal-terminated surfaces exhibit no reconstruction, and their broken-bond states are located in the vicinity of the valence band maxima (VBM), pinning the Fermi level. items.title: Quantifying Blinking Suppression and Probing Its Mechanism in PPD-Treated Single Quantum Dots
items.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. While recent advances have enabled partial or complete suppression of this effect, both the degree of suppression and the mechanism by which it occurs are often difficult to establish. In the present work we analyse the blinking suppression of single CdSe/ZnS QDs after treatment with p-phenylenediamine (PPD), recently discovered by Yang et al. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. For data analysis we apply a threshold-free two-dimensional criterion recently proposed by Podshivaylov and Frantsuzov. The criterion is based on the relative quantum yield estimator $\...

items.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
items.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. The strongest general-purpose model scores only 53.7%, and on matched...

items.title: Unifying dynamical electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions from first principles
items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. A fully dynamical treatment of metals and doped semiconductors within time-dependent density functional perturbation theory (TDDFPT) is expensive and numerically delicate. Here, we introduce DFPT+A downfolding ("A" for active space), which starts from the static density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) response of a computationally convenient base system and adds the dynamical screening of a low-energy active space, described by Wannier functions. The required statically screened electron-electron interaction is computed using DFPT directly in the basis of Wannier-function pairs and truncated in a computationally efficient and systematically improvable way. The...

items.title: Evaluating Structural and SAT Attack Resilience in Cryptographic Dynamic Logic Locking via Keystream Capping
items.abstract: Untrusted third-party entities throughout the semiconductor supply chain expose proprietary hardware intellectual property to reverse engineering, piracy, and overproduction. While logic locking counters this threat by embedding key-dependent logic, conventional static key-gates remain vulnerable to both oracle-guided SAT attacks and structural removal attacks due to their time-invariant netlist signatures. Dynamic schemes such as STREAMLOCK mitigate oracle attacks by continuously masking signals with cryptographic keystream, achieving near 50\% Hamming distance output corruption under incorrect keys with low hardware overhead. However, confining key-gates to primary outputs leaves internal combinational cones vulnerable to single-tap structural bypasses. This work extends dynamic logic locking by distributing key-gates within internal paths prioritized via fault-propagation analysis. Th...

items.title: 10 kV $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Sub-Bandgap Triggered Impurity Photoconductive Semiconductor Switches (i-PCSSs): Lessons for Optimal Design
items.abstract: $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are attractive for high-voltage operation, but above-bandgap triggering requires deep-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we investigate a 650-um-thick, 0.01% Fe-doped $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ impurity PCSS with a 5-mm lateral gap under continuous-wave (CW) 808-nm sub-bandgap excitation at biases up to 10 kV ( 20 kV cm^-1). The device exhibited clear sub-bandgap photoconductive switching. As the optical power density increased from 0.64 to 3.18 W cm^-2, the ON-state current increased progressively while the ON-state resistance decreased, consistent with enhanced defect-assisted photocarrier generation. A higher applied bias further strengthened the switching response through enhanced field-assisted carrier transport. The ON/OFF ratio increases with optical power density but exhibits a nonmonotonic bias dependence, reaching approximately 15-...

items.title: Complete Au-free Metallization Platform for UWBG Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N channel MOS-HEMTs using Ti/Al/Ti Ohmic Contacts and Refractory TiN/Pt Gates
items.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. items.title: Efficient Simulation of Gate Leakage Currents in Ultra-scaled Transistors from First Principles
items.abstract: To ensure high electrostatic integrity in ultra-scaled field-effect transistors (FETs), thin gate dielectric layers are typically needed, potentially giving rise to (strong) leakage currents. Being able to model this effect is therefore crucial. Here, we show how gate leakage currents can be computed at the ab initio level in WS$_2$-hBN FETs by extending the well-established quantum transmitting boundary method (QTBM). Two main challenges are tackled: (i) the calculation of the open boundary conditions (OBCs) for the gate contacts and (ii) the solution of the resulting sparse linear system of equations A x = b where the matrix A possesses an unstructured sparsity pattern. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state of the art and can be readily applied to simulate transistors with gate lengths exceeding 25 nm.

We identify the origins of both negative and positive MRR components and connect them to interlayer and intralayer spin-dependent transport mechanisms. items.title: Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis: integrating reinforcement learning and conformal prediction for reliable wafer defect classification
items.abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is a complex, multi-step process that requires both high precision and low operating costs. Therefore, detecting defects in a high-volume setting is an important component of wafer map analysis for reliable production. However, most state-of-the-art deep learning approaches require a full scan of the surface, which hinders the development of high-throughput inspection systems. To address this problem, we propose Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis (UFLD), a novel algorithm that employs reinforcement learning for adaptive measurement acquisition and provides a prediction uncertainty level after each step, stopping the process once sufficient information is obtained. items.abstract: Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. Being nearly lattice-matched and moreover highly resistant to lattice and bond distortions thanks to a largely covalent bonding, cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te sets a benchmark to test the sensitivity of lattice vibrations to minimum lattice and bond distortions induced by alloying. items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. Phase purity in terms of n is crucial towards narrow emission bands and the design of band structure alignment for charge carrier funneling. We present a simple and scalable synthesis method using cesium and butylammonium as A-cations to fabricate microcrystal powders of 2D lead bromide perovskites that results in samples with very high n-phase purity. The obtained microcrystals show a sharp onset in absorbance and single narrow emission peak in UV-blue spectral range, and we confirm their structure and composition with X-ray diffraction and energy dispersive spectroscopy. items.title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
items.abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. items.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
items.abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. items.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. items.abstract: This paper presents the circuit-level implementation of a mismatch-tolerant high-gain operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using automatic negative-conductance calibration in 65-nm CMOS. The technique enhances OTA gain by compensating for its finite output conductance using a cross-coupled transistor pair, with an on-chip calibration loop that eliminates the need for a replica circuit or external tuning. The calibration routine increases the gain by driving the steady state error of the OTA in a unity gain feedback loop toward zero. The implementation addresses practical challenges involving comparator offset, DAC design, and subtractor gain and offset. items.title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin--photon interfaces for scalable quantum networks require bright optical transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent spin control. Donor spins in direct-bandgap semiconductors combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate coherent optical control of a single Cl donor electron spin in ZnSe. Resonant excitation reveals spin relaxation dynamics and measures spin coherence through coherent population trapping (CPT). Off-resonant ultrafast pulses are implemented to drive spin Rabi oscillations and demonstrate Ramsey interference. Multiple dark resonances in the CPT spectrum further reveal hyperfine coupling between the electron and the I=3/2 Cl nucleus. Together, these results demonstrate the first c...

items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. items.title: Residual AM and PM Noise of Selected X-Band Amplifiers
items.abstract: In microwave systems design, amplitude modulation (AM) noise is often ignored relative to phase modulation (PM) noise. However, in high-performance applications requiring ultra-low PM noise, AM noise becomes a critical limiting factor due to AM-to-PM conversion mechanisms. Because AM noise specifications are rarely, if ever, provided for commercial microwave components, this study characterizes the residual AM and PM noise of several 10 GHz amplifiers. We present performance data for various Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) amplifier designs and demonstrate the noise reduction achieved through power-summed configurations. For example, a discrete-die GaAs HBT amplifier achieves residual PM noise below $-160$ dBrad$^2$/Hz and AM noise of approximately $-155$ dB/Hz at a 1 kHz offset in a quad power-summed configuration. A notable finding is that the majority of amplifier designs surv...

items.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
items.abstract: In this letter, we develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) for the calculation of local electronic observables. The method couples the spatial decay of the density matrix with a hierarchy of Fourier probes, improving accuracy through refinement, and making use of all previously evaluated responses. The variation in the calculated observables during the refinement process carries information on the residual error. We use a locality-based model to estimate the error from these changes with no extra probing calculations. In particular, we demonstrate the method for electron densities and nonlocal pseudopotential forces for fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians of semiconductors, metals and thermally perturbed silica. The convergence is significantly accelerated by the spatial decay of the density matrix, especially if the density matrix is short-ranged. The number of probes necessary to...

items.title: Laser-Induced Rashba Spin-Orbit Torques in Multiferroic Semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te
items.abstract: The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling, and carrier-mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge0.85Mn0.15Te using time-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser-induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin-orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser-induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba split, spin-locked valence band states and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. items.title: Uncertainty and Business-Aware Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Semiconductor Manufacturing
items.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimates guide maintenance in semiconductor manufacturing, where a late intervention can disrupt production but an early one discards usable equipment life. A single prediction does not express the uncertainty needed to choose between these outcomes. We combine Deep Learning (DL) sequence models with Simoultaneous Quantile Regression (SQR) to estimate RUL at selectable quantile levels, and evaluate maintenance decisions using Unexpected Breaks (UB), Unexploited Lifetime (UL), and a cost-weighted objective. On the $F_1$ fault mode of the 2018 PHM Data Challenge (PHM18) ion-milling dataset, we compare recurrent, Transformer, and State Space Models (SSM) architectures. Diagonal State Spaced (S4D) gives the strongest overall RUL accuracy across the evaluated quantiles. Varying the quantile and maintenance window exposes the trade-off between failure risk and earl...

items.title: Transport-Noise and Optical Witnesses of Electronic Multipartite Entanglement
items.abstract: Entanglement among particles distinguishes correlated quantum materials from conventional metals and semiconductors. Experimentally certifying intrinsic entanglement among interacting electrons in materials is important not only for classifying states of matter, but also for developing material-based quantum technologies. Here, we introduce a transport protocol for witnessing multipartite entanglement from the equilibrium current-noise spectrum, measured directly or reconstructed from optical conductivity. The appropriately integrated, symmetrized, and projected noise spectrum obeys an upper bound derived from microscopic model parameters. Unlike witnesses based on localized spins, our framework applies to general electronic states without requiring magnetic moments and remains invariant under single-particle basis transformations.
